To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the renormalization of a given QFT is independent on the value of the temperature, and the FTFT is renormalized by the same procedure of QFT.

(a) the ultraviolet divergent terms in FTFT can be expressed in terms of the T = 0 divergent terms and the temperature; (b) in FTFT the ultraviolet diverging terms are independent of the temperature; (c) the ultraviolet renormalized T = 0 theory is also ultraviolet renormalizable in FTFT.
the renormalization in FTFT is not a problem of ultraviolet divergencies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the problem of renomalization in FTFT.
the study of the ultraviolet divergent structure of the effective action for a scalar field theory in finite temperature field theories.
the study of the microlocal analysis in the FTFT and its applications in the problem of renomalization in FTFT, and in the derivation of the renormalization group equations for the FTFT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ultraviolet divergent terms in FTFT are the same of those of T = 0 theory and the only effect of temperature on the renormalization procedure is to introduce a finite temperature dependent renormalization scale.
, for a given QFT, the ultraviolet divergent behavior is the same for both T = 0, and FTFT theories.
the ultraviolet behavior is the same in both cases, the T = 0 QFT and its FTFT version.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ultraviolet behavior of a FTFT is completely determined by the T = 0 theory.

we have found a way to define the finite temperature Green function in a mathematically rigorous way, which is free from the ambiguities of the usual perturbation theory, and which is consistent with the usual perturbative expansion.
the renormalization in FTFT is a problem of microlocal analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ultraviolet divergent contributions in the FTFT come from the same distributions as those of the QFT.
the renormalization of the FTFT is not a new issue but rather a generalization of the QFT renormalization procedure.
we are able to provide a rigorous mathematical derivation of the standard perturbative results in the FTFT.
